content: Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the likelihood of severe side effects. This document does not include all potential drug interactions. It is essential to maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this list with your healthcare provider and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. If the situation is less critical, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as viral load and T-cell counts, are necessary to monitor your condition and the medication's effectiveness. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication in its original packaging at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Keep the desiccant (drying agent) in the bottle and ensure the bottle is tightly closed when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in July 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete details about this product and your individual health needs. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Treatment may reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and this medication may be part of that treatment plan. This medication can pass into breast milk.
